task.description: REVIEWER (WF-02 Step 2d) hard gate on REQ-158 commit 019c050 -- idiom, legacy-path maintainability, scope, decision-record consistency, test quality.
acceptance_criteria: Idiom verdict on compute_hash/2's length-prefixed framing implementation
Idiom assessment of the legacy bare-binary script_ref backward-compat path
Confirm no scope creep vs REQ-158's requirements.yaml entry
Test quality confirmed across both test files, including the rework's security regression tests

findings.detail: length_prefixed/1 (<<byte_size(field)::32>> <> field) is a clean, standard Elixir binary-construction idiom -- no manual byte-walking, no awkward Enum tricks. compute_hash/2 composes it via a plain pipeline (Capabilities.new/1 |> Enum.to_list/1 |> Enum.sort/1 |> Enum.map(&length_prefixed/1) |> IO.iodata_to_binary/1) followed by a single <> concatenation and :crypto.hash/2 |> Base.encode16(case: :lower). Not a workaround; this is the standard way to build an unambiguous binary frame in Elixir.

findings.verdict: acceptable as implemented, with one documentation gap worth a light follow-up (non-blocking)
findings.detail: normalize_script_ref/1 is implemented as two function-head clauses (bare binary() vs the %{manifest:, script_source:} map) dispatching via pattern matching, not a case/if doing the state machine's job by hand -- this is the idiomatic Elixir shape for a widened input type, and decision 0014 explicitly deferred script_ref's concrete shape to S5, so widening it here is exactly what that record anticipated, not a contradiction. The moduledoc documents both shapes and the empty-manifest treatment of the legacy path clearly (lines 8-17). What is missing: neither the moduledoc nor the @typedoc marks the bare-binary shape as legacy/deprecated for *future* callers, only as a backward-compat concession for existing ones -- a new caller reading the @type script_ref union today has no textual signal to prefer the manifest-carrying shape. Recommend (non-blocking, can be a follow-up doc-only touch by ELIXIR-DEV or folded into the next Lua requirement that adds a script_ref caller): add one sentence to the script_ref @typedoc or moduledoc explicitly steering new callers to the map shape and noting the bare-binary form exists only for the ~40 pre-REQ-158 call sites. A wrapper/adapter function is not warranted -- normalize_script_ref/1 already IS that adapter, cleanly, at the one place it's needed.

git show 48b147b --stat and 019c050 --stat confirm changes are confined to lib/letflow/engine/lua/manifest.ex (new), lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex (script_ref widening + compute_hash call site), test/letflow/engine/lua/{manifest_test.exs (new), manifest_executor_audit_test.exs (new), executor_test.exs (updated hash assertions + new map-shape describe block)}, plus handoff files. All match REQ-158's requirements.yaml scope items 1-4 exactly (manifest representation, load-time validation, feeding LuaScriptAudit's existing INV-LSA-2 check rather than reimplementing it, moduledoc hash-coverage statement). No new abstraction (behaviour, macro, generic plumbing) introduced ahead of need.

decision 0014 (line ~171, ~293) explicitly states script_ref resolves to a concrete type only once S5 fixes it -- REQ-158 widening executor.ex's script_ref type is exactly that fixing, not a silent re-decision. No contradiction found against REQ-153 (Executor isolation -- unaffected, still a fresh Lua.t() per call), REQ-154/155/156 (instruction budget / wallclock / heap limit -- run_script/run_with_heap_limit signatures changed only to thread manifest through, enforcement logic untouched), or REQ-157 (Capabilities -- Manifest.to_grant_set/1 delegates to Capabilities.new/1 as the single conversion point, no duplicate capability-set logic introduced).

manifest_test.exs and manifest_executor_audit_test.exs are well-organized (numbered describe blocks tracking AC numbers), names state the exact property proven (e.g. 'a capability string containing an embedded LF does not collide with the equivalent split list'), and assertions carry inline failure-message context explaining *why* a match matters, not just that it must hold. The two rework regression tests (delimiter-injection LF collision, NUL-byte framing) directly reproduce SECURITY-REVIEWER's found collision and a plausible analogous one, not a weakened proxy. No sleep/timing dependence, no shared mutable state, real Postgres-backed integration tests use per-test schema provisioning with on_exit cleanup (async: false, correctly, since Postgres schema lifecycle is shared) -- not flaky by construction. Pure tests in manifest_test.exs correctly run async: true.

result.notes: No Elixir toolchain available in this review environment (mix: command not found) -- verdict relies on ELIXIR-DEV's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's quoted real mix test/mix compile --warnings-as-errors output (2187/2187 passing, clean compile, both commits) rather than an independent re-run. This is disclosed per core-directives.md rather than silently assumed.
